decisions.intent: Apply one link-menu edit to every link generated by the same inline-mark operation and persist all changed blocks as one undoable transaction.

preconditions: The user opens a Protyle inline link menu for one link or for a caller-supplied group of link elements.
A group spanning multiple blocks supplies the pre-edit HTML for every target block.
stateTransitions: A Zod-backed CaliburRouter partitions the close state into no change, current-block update, and captured multi-block update.
Title and href edits apply to every supplied link element; an all-empty form removes every supplied link element.
A current-block update preserves the established updateTransaction owner; a captured multi-block update emits matched forward and undo operations through one transaction.
outputs: All changed link elements receive the submitted title and href while the existing primary-anchor editing behavior remains unchanged.
Plugins receive content-free user-operation intent events for toolbar link toggles and persisted link-menu updates.
invariants: No unchanged close creates a transaction or emits a link-menu update intent.
A multi-block call without captured baselines, a changed block without an old HTML entry, or a block without data-node-id fails explicitly before a partial persistence transaction.
S-Forge's existing setInlineMark cross-block range normalization is not changed by this series.
failures: Clipboard inspection errors are logged explicitly and the existing selected-text link path continues without fabricating clipboard content.
A missing toolbar range exits before link mutation.

testEvidence: pnpm exec vitest --run test/protyle/linkMenuSavePlan.test.ts test/protyle/keydownDeleteRouter.test.ts test/protyle/keydownDeleteMiddleware.test.ts (3 files, 7 tests passed)
pnpm test (Node 256 tests and all Vitest shards passed)
pnpm typecheck reports zero diagnostics in this series' changed files; repository-wide baseline diagnostics remain explicit
notes: Semantic commit 89d7b17d11faf74d23074b27ea4e4d06c2b6c2c9 maps the upstream link-menu API to S-Forge's split menu, toolbar, transaction, and intent owners.
